Gamut

GAM-ut · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Gamut is the complete range or scope of something.

The new restaurant's menu runs the gamut from simple grilled cheese to elaborate seven-course tasting plates.

Worked Example

During the trial, the witness's testimony ran the gamut from confident and detailed to confused and contradictory within a single afternoon.

Gamut almost always appears in the phrase 'run the gamut,' describing something that covers every possibility from one extreme to another.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — variety → entirety → gamut

variety vs. gamut

variety vs. gamut: Variety just means having different kinds of something -- it doesn't necessarily mean covering every possible extreme.

entirety vs. gamut

entirety vs. gamut: Entirety goes further still, meaning absolutely all of something, leaving out nothing whatsoever.

Build the Word

The pieces

origin — gamma ut

origin — gamma ut: the lowest note of the medieval musical scale (Medieval Latin, from Greek letter gamma + the note 'ut')

Put it together

Put it together: Gamut began as a medieval music term -- gamma ut, the very lowest note on the old musical scale -- and came to mean the entire scale of notes, then any complete range of anything at all.

Where it comes from

Where it comes from: Gamut fuses two medieval music syllables: gamma (the Greek letter, used as a note name) and ut (the lowest note of the old scale). The name of that single bottom note stretched to cover the whole run of notes, and then any complete range you can imagine.
